title: The Charge Up the Hill
craft_focus: short sentences that speed the action and hold the reader in the moment

source.basis: Adapted from Theodore Roosevelt, The Rough Riders (1899), under DESIGN_RULES 2.5.
source.attribution: Theodore Roosevelt. The Rough Riders. 1899. Project Gutenberg eBook #13000, https://www.gutenberg.org/ebooks/13000, accessed 2026-11-11. Public domain in the United States.
source.adaptation: Extracted a single 343-word passage (Chapter IV, the climb up Kettle Hill); the authoring pass will split long sentences and drop rare words; no facts added.
source.survey: One paragraph of the Kettle Hill charge: the men cheering as they run, Roosevelt riding up the lane, the wire fence, and the last shots at the top.

notes: Anchor: Chapter IV, 'The Cavalry at Santiago', the paragraph beginning 'By this time we were all in the spirit of the thing'. CRAFT RISK - the short-sentence construct is NOT visible verbatim: the 13 sentences average 26.4 words and measure FK 11.1, because Roosevelt chains clauses with commas and semicolons. The paragraph is split-ready, not short-sentenced. Clause joins that become short sentences: 'By this time we were all in the spirit of the thing and greatly excited by the charge' -> 'We were all in the spirit of it. The charge excited us.'; 'Some forty yards from the top I ran into a wire fence and jumped off Little Texas, turning him loose.' -> 'Forty yards from the top I hit a wire fence. I jumped off Little Texas and turned him loose.'; 'As I ran up to the hill, Bardshar stopped to shoot, and two Spaniards fell as he emptied his magazine.' -> 'Bardshar stopped to shoot. Two Spaniards fell.' Splitting to about 12-word sentences should land near FK 5.5 (estimate). If the authoring pass does not split, this text cannot teach the assigned construct and a source with native short sentences should replace it.
